questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to study in an English-speaking country and I wanted to make sure that I was able to go despite Covid.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Scan Design Foundation (SDF) was a big help and the University provided a guided tour for international students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty difficult, SDF tried their best to help but many had a hard time finding housing. I lived in a shared apartment with other international students through WESLI Short-Term Housing. Housing can be quite exprensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Don't stay too far away from downtown - not more than 4 km I would say. However, you do get a free bus card and the bus system is decent. SDF also provides bicycles for people who live far from campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to follow the guide.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could send an email and they would respond pretty fast.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didnøt have any problems at all.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register when registration opens so the courses you want to take don't get filled up. You can always drop classes later. Keep in mind that campus is pretty big so make sure you can get from one class to the next in time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They varied a lot in difficulty but in general, they were easier than back home. If you want to learn a lot I would recommend not taking courses that are only for undergraduates.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The lectures were very similar but they tracked attendance in many of the classes. More assignments are also to be expected as well as more grading.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
303 Biology of Microorganisms
528 Immunology
640 General Virology-Multiplication of Viruses
703 Carcinogenesis and Tumor Cell Biology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
703 - very relevant assignments, no exam, pretty chill.
528 - learned a lot, multiple choice exams
640 - probably the most interesting in my opinion (the exams were however more difficult than the others)
303 - probably my least favorite because it was too easy, but good if you want a lot of freedom and still pass

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Visa was more expensive than expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general, things were more expensive because of the exchange rate at the time I arrived. More specifically I would say groceries. Going out is less expensive (note: Whiskey Jack's have 25-cent rail drinks every Thursday)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were over a hundred clubs with whatever you can imagine. Almost every day the university also had events, often with free food included.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to a football game to get the experience.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Plan trips to Devil's Lake, Minneapolis, Chicago etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was not too difficult.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get a buddy through the SDF programme, join a club or socialize with people in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not anything specific. People wore a lot of gym clothes to school. Also, remember tipping.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed game days a lot. Football is a big part of the culture and not just watching the sport but also tailgating before.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Bring a warm winter jacket and thermal underwear to keep warm during winter
2. Attend as many events as possible (mainly at the beggining)
3. Plan trips to explore more of the US.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bring a lot of rye bread and put it in your freezer.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new international friends and going on self-arranged trips with other students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I shared my bedroom with another international exchange student and even though we got along very well, sometimes I needed a private space that I didn't have.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
